skills.contract:
---
name: compendium-batch
description: Operating contract for working a batch of compendium items unattended (IDEA-1091) — one git worktree per batch on a local checkout, one sanctioned command per intent, deterministic preflight, and exactly one deliverable, a draft PR from the batch branch or a plain-text report. Use when handed a selection command or an ID list to process without a human in the loop, whether as a hosted bg-compendium run or the long-running local-model agent.
---

# Compendium batch — operating contract

You work a **batch** of compendium items. The batch loop, the write surface, and the deliverable are the same regardless of which model or framework runs you. Design rationale: `docs/research/2026-08-28-IDEA-1091-agent-instructions-and-workflows.md`.

## Output contract

A batch produces exactly one of:

| Artifact                                                        | When                                                                | Shape                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Draft PR** from branch `agent/batch-<id>`                     | preflight green and the diff is non-empty                           | `gh pr create --draft --title "<batch-id>: <batch type>" --body-file <manifest>`; body = batch manifest + the full preflight output |
| **Plain-text report** at `$COMPENDIUM_REPORT_DIR/<batch-id>.md` | anything else — empty diff, a check failed, an item needs judgement | fixed headings below                                                                                                                |

Nothing else leaves the worktree. No OV sync, no index edits on a machine branch, no ClickUp/Slack/Notion, no direct pushes to `main`, `pop`, or `workbook`.

## Batch loop

1. **Select** — the batch input is a selection command or an explicit ID list handed to you. Never choose items from your own judgement.
2. **Isolate** — `git -C ~/code/compendium fetch origin && git -C ~/code/compendium worktree add .claude/worktrees/batch-<id> -b agent/batch-<id> origin/<machine-branch>`. All work happens under that path; export `WORKTREE` to it and `cd` there.
3. **Ground truth** — `uv run python _scripts/build-lane-records.py --type-dir <type> --output <records.json.gz>` for verbatim `summary` / `body_excerpt` per entry. Never re-derive what you are about to edit (TASK-1161 lesson).
4. **Work** — one item at a time, using only the commands in the table below and the batch-type skill you were given.
5. **Preflight** — in this order: `uv run python _scripts/lint-frontmatter.py --files <files>` → `uv run python _scripts/check-bare-fences.py <files>` → `uv run python _scripts/rebuild-indexes.py --fix` → `pre-commit run --files <changed>`.
6. **Deliver** — green: `git add <paths> && git commit -m "<batch-id>: <type> — <n> items" -- <paths>` → `git push -u origin agent/batch-<id>` → draft PR. Not green: write the report.
7. **Clean up** — `git -C ~/code/compendium worktree remove .claude/worktrees/batch-<id>`; never leave a worktree behind.

## One command per intent

| Intent                       | Command                                                                                                                                                              | Never                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Find an item / related items | `compendium-preflight "<query>" --budget 60`                                                                                                                         | raw `rg`/`grep`/`find` over the vault, `ov find` by hand |
| List by frontmatter filter   | `uv run python _scripts/compendium-lookup.py list --type <t> --status <s> --limit 50`                                                                                | reading `index.md` to discover items                     |
| Read an item                 | `Read` the absolute path preflight printed                                                                                                                           | `cat`/`sed`, guessing a path from an ID                  |
| Get ground truth for a batch | `uv run python _scripts/build-lane-records.py --type-dir <type> --output <file>`                                                                                     | paraphrasing from memory                                 |
| Change a status              | edit exactly `status:` and `date_updated:`; append one dated note under the last body section                                                                        | `obsidian property:set`, moving the file                 |
| Complete an item             | `uv run python _scripts/complete-item.py <ID> --status <s> --ref "<receipt>"` (dry run) then `--apply` — only when `check-closability.py` reports `ALL-CRITERIA-MET` | deciding closability from prose                          |
| Create an item               | `compendium-new --vault "$WORKTREE" --type … --title … --repo …` — only when the batch input names the item to create                                                | `next-id.sh` for allocation, hand-written IDs            |
| Edit a `retrieval_summary`   | single-line plain scalar, ≤200 chars, no double quotes, no colon-then-space, no space-then-hash, no leading digit (IMPR-1105 schema)                                 | block scalars, quoting                                   |
| Add a cross-link             | `uv run python _scripts/add-related.py <ID> --link <OTHER-ID>` (dry run) then `--apply`; `--both` only when the pair is mutual                                       | hand-editing `related:`                                  |
| Regenerate indexes           | `uv run python _scripts/rebuild-indexes.py --fix`                                                                                                                    | editing any `index.md`                                   |
| Validate                     | `pre-commit run --files <changed>`                                                                                                                                   | skipping hooks, `--no-verify`                            |
| Deliver                      | `git commit -- <paths>` → `git push -u origin agent/batch-<id>` → `gh pr create --draft`                                                                             | `git add -A`, bare `git commit`, `git stash`, force-push |
| Cannot proceed               | write the report and stop                                                                                                                                            | retrying with a guess                                    |

## Hard stops

Any schema failure, merge conflict, script error, missing file, or ambiguity is a hard stop: put the raw output in the report and move to the next item. You may self-fix only single-correct-resolution failures — a formatter rewrite, a missing fence language tag, trailing whitespace, re-adding a file a hook modified. Never guess at a status, an ID, a wikilink target, or a summary. Two failed edits on one file is the limit; the second attempt must be built from bytes you have read, not a reworded guess.

## Out of reach (hosted-session-only, TASK-1185)

Renames, index restructures, compaction and compaction PRs, OV reconcile or sync, cross-type batch edits, anything under `.claude/`, `_scripts/`, `_templates/`, and the intake discuss gate (you never file an item from your own judgement).

## Report format

```markdown
# <batch-id> — <batch type>

## Batch

<selection command or ID list; machine branch; worktree path; started/finished>

## Attempted

| ID | Action | Result |

## Preflight

<raw output of every check, verbatim>

## Delivered

<PR URL, or "none">

## Needs a human

- <ID> — <one line> — <raw check output>
```

## Batch types

| Skill                                 | Selection                                                          | Pass condition                            | Deliverable              |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `compendium-batch-summary-repair`     | `lint-frontmatter.py` long/quoted `retrieval_summary` findings     | `lint-frontmatter.py --files` clean       | draft PR per ≤20 entries |
| `compendium-batch-fence-repair`       | `check-bare-fences.py` findings                                    | `check-bare-fences.py` clean on the files | draft PR                 |
| `compendium-batch-closability-report` | `check-closability.py --type <t> --days <n> [--match <re>] --json` | n/a — report only                         | report                   |
skills.summary:
---
name: compendium-batch-summary-repair
description: Batch type for the compendium batch agent — repair retrieval_summary values that fail the IMPR-1105 schema (over 200 chars, quoted, block scalar, contains ": " or "#", leading digit) so lint-frontmatter passes, without changing what the summary asserts. Runs under the compendium-batch contract; deliverable is a draft PR per ≤20 entries.
---

# Batch type: `retrieval_summary` repair

Follow `compendium-batch` for the loop, the worktree, preflight, and delivery. This skill only defines selection, the edit rule, and the pass condition.

## Selection

Inside the worktree:

```bash
uv run python _scripts/lint-frontmatter.py --quiet
```

Take only findings of the summary kinds: `long retrieval_summary (>200)`, quoted / block-scalar summary, or a summary containing a colon followed by a space, a space followed by a hash sign, or starting with a digit. Ignore every other finding kind — they are not this batch. Cap a batch at 20 entries; more than that is a second batch.

## Ground truth

```bash
uv run python _scripts/build-lane-records.py --type-dir <type> --output "$WORKTREE/.batch/records.json.gz"
```

The record's `summary` is the current value; `body_excerpt` is the entry. Edit from these, never from memory.

## Edit rule

Rewrite the summary so that it:

- is one line, a plain YAML scalar (no `"`, no `>-`/`|`), ≤200 characters;
- contains no colon-followed-by-space sequence (a bare colon is fine), no space-followed-by-hash, and does not start with a digit;
- keeps every item ID, PR number, date, version string, and backticked token that the current summary contains — dropping one is a failure, not a shortening;
- states the same outcome as the current summary. Shorten by removing filler, not facts. If the current summary has no outcome and the body does, you may add the outcome in ≤12 words; if you are unsure what the outcome is, do not edit — report the entry instead.

Edit only the `retrieval_summary:` line. Do not touch `date_updated` (a summary repair is not new information — same rule as compaction).

## Pass condition

```bash
uv run python _scripts/lint-frontmatter.py --files <edited files>
```

must report 0 findings for those files, and every ID/PR/date/version token present in the old summary must still be present in the new one (check the diff line by line before committing). Then the standard preflight and delivery from `compendium-batch`.

## Report items, do not edit

- The entry was updated in the last 48 hours (someone is writing it).
- The current summary and the body disagree about the outcome.
- The summary cannot reach ≤200 characters without dropping a token.

---
name: compendium-batch-fence-repair
description: Batch type for the compendium batch agent — add a language tag to bare opening code fences (MD040) that check-bare-fences.py flags, using the fence's content to choose the tag and "text" when unsure. Runs under the compendium-batch contract; deliverable is one draft PR.
---

# Batch type: bare code fence repair

Follow `compendium-batch` for the loop, the worktree, preflight, and delivery. This skill only defines selection, the edit rule, and the pass condition.

## Selection

Inside the worktree, per type directory named in the batch input:

```bash
uv run python _scripts/check-bare-fences.py <type-dir>/**/*.md
```

Each finding is a file and a line with a bare opening fence. The checker is fence-state-aware (PR #107): a line it does **not** flag is either already tagged or a closing fence — never add a tag to a line the checker did not name.

## Edit rule

Replace the bare opening fence on the flagged line with a tagged one:

| Content that follows the fence                          | Tag      |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| shell commands, `$`/`#` prompts, `kubectl`/`git`/`curl` | `bash`   |
| YAML keys, k8s manifests                                | `yaml`   |
| JSON                                                    | `json`   |
| Python                                                  | `python` |
| SQL                                                     | `sql`    |
| a stack trace, log lines, tables, prose, anything else  | `text`   |

Change only the fence line. Never touch the fence's content, the closing fence, or anything else in the file. Do not bump `date_updated`.

## Pass condition

```bash
uv run python _scripts/check-bare-fences.py <edited files>
```

must report 0 findings, and `pre-commit run --files <edited files>` must pass `markdownlint-cli2`. Then the standard preflight and delivery from `compendium-batch`.

## Report items, do not edit

- The flagged line is inside another fence (nested / quad-fence files — IDEA-1083's "doubled-closer" cases need a human).
- The file changed in the last 48 hours.

# BUG-152 — Standard date fields display as #inst Clojure literals when not mapped to question keys

Date-typed standard fields submitted via DipDash/Mage to the ACL platform display as raw Clojure `#inst` instant literals instead of formatted dates on claim detail pages.

---

# Problem

When viewing claim details on the ACL platform (e.g. [People claim 9e2c5a10](https://dashboard.aclaimant.com/customers/people/companies/273999/incidents/claims/9e2c5a10-5dcf-11f1-ad87-472f85ea4994/details)), date-typed standard fields show raw Clojure `#inst` formatting like `#inst "2024-01-15T00:00:00.000-00:00"` instead of a human-readable date format.

These fields come from the Aclaimant standard field mappings in DipDash (`auto_generate=TRUE` in `common.standard_format_fields`). Per Mark Nicolosi (platform team lead): claims and claim extensions do not use input maps — this is a platform UI rendering bug, same class as a recent litigation flag display issue.

Reported by Amie Johnson for the People/peoplease_ccmsi_claim_ingestion pipeline.

- Slack: <https://aclaimant.slack.com/archives/C08Q7S22NGG/p1781803068416739>
- Claim: <https://dashboard.aclaimant.com/customers/people/companies/273999/incidents/claims/9e2c5a10-5dcf-11f1-ad87-472f85ea4994/details>
- Pipeline: <https://data.aclaimant.com/pipelines/people/peoplease_ccmsi_claim_ingestion>

# Root Cause

The pipeline correctly formats dates — the issue is in how the platform renders unmapped standard fields.

**Pipeline side (not at fault):**

1. DipDash's `standard_format_fields` table defines 36 date-typed fields with `auto_generate=TRUE` and empty `format` values
2. Mage's dbt `to_date` macro (`to_date.sql`) converts all date fields to `YYYY-MM-DD` strings via Snowflake `to_char`
3. The answer JSON payload (`int_standard_format_answers.sql`) places these as clean string values like `"2024-01-15"`
4. Python submission layer (`answers.py`) passes values through unchanged — only transforms underscore keys to hyphenated keys

**Platform side (at fault):**

1. The ACL platform's Clojure backend receives the `YYYY-MM-DD` date strings
2. Claims and claim extensions do NOT use input maps (confirmed by Mark Nicolosi) — so the input map hypothesis was incorrect
3. The platform UI simply does not format date values on claim/claim-extension fields — it displays the raw Clojure `#inst` serialization of the stored `java.util.Date`
4. This is the same class of bug as a recently reported litigation flag display issue — the UI is not type-aware for these fields

# Investigation Notes

- 2026-06-18: Amie reported in #help-dipdash-questions. Investigated full pipeline chain from DipDash standard_format_fields through Mage dbt macros to platform submission. Confirmed zero `#inst` references in DipDash or Mage codebases — the literal originates from the platform's Clojure backend.
- Searched compendium vault for prior `#inst`, Clojure date, input map, and platform rendering issues — no duplicates found.
- 806 of 807 standard format fields have `auto_generate=TRUE`. 36 are date-typed (`date`, `date-time`, `time`). All have empty `format` values in the seed CSV.
- 2026-06-18: Mark Nicolosi (platform) clarified: claims and claim extensions do NOT use input maps. The `#inst` display is a platform UI rendering bug — same class as a recent litigation flag display issue. Amie filed OWL-19704.

# Fix

Platform UI fix — the claim/claim-extension detail view needs type-aware rendering for date fields instead of displaying raw Clojure `#inst` serialization. Amie filed ClickUp ticket OWL-19704 for the platform team.

# Verification

To be determined — pending fix approach selection.

# Related

- Cross-links to other bugs: none identified
- Key files investigated:
  - DipDash: `api/seed-data/real-production/standard_format_fields.csv`
  - DipDash: `web/src/utils/columnMappingUtils.tsx:322` (`getCombinedMappings`)
  - Mage: `dbt/data_ingestion_automation/macros/to_date.sql`
  - Mage: `dbt/data_ingestion_automation/models/data_driven/data_driven_map_columns_to_asf.sql`
  - Mage: `dbt/data_ingestion_automation/models/standardformat/intermediate/int_standard_format_answers.sql`
  - Mage: `ingest/answers.py`

# Sources

- Slack thread: <https://aclaimant.slack.com/archives/C08Q7S22NGG/p1781803068416739>

# INFO-1113 --- Claude Code Configuration — CLAUDE.md, settings.json, Permissions, Auto Mode

Reference for the full `.claude/` configuration surface — directory layout and precedence, CLAUDE.md and auto memory, settings.json structure, permission rules and modes, auto mode basics, and the debug workflow for when config isn't taking effect. Distilled from the official Claude Code docs (`claude-directory.md`, `memory.md`, `settings.md`, `permissions.md`, `permission-modes.md`, `auto-mode-config.md`, `debug-your-config.md`). Core reference for anyone authoring skills/config in the dotfiles repo — this vault's own root `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/settings.json`/`.claude/settings.local.json` are a live worked example of everything below (referenced only, not altered by this entry).

---

# Answer

## `.claude/` directory layout

Both a project's `.claude/` and `~/.claude/` (user-level) follow the same shape:

| Path | Purpose | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CLAUDE.md` (repo root or `.claude/CLAUDE.md`) | Project instructions loaded every session | Project |
| `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Personal preferences for all projects | User |
| `CLAUDE.local.md` | Personal, gitignored project overrides | Project (local) |
| `.claude/rules/*.md` | Modular instruction files, optionally path-scoped via YAML `paths:` frontmatter | Project or user |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Team-shared permissions, hooks, env, statusLine, model | Project (committed) |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Personal project overrides (gitignored) | Project (local) |
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | Personal global settings | User |
| `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Invokable prompt + bundled files, `/name` or auto-invoked | Project or user (`~/.claude/skills/`) |
| `.claude/commands/*.md` | Legacy single-file `/name` prompts (skills supersede these; a same-named skill wins) | Project or user |
| `.claude/agents/*.md` | Subagent definitions with their own tools | Project or user |
| `.mcp.json` | Project-scoped MCP servers (require approval on first trust) | Project |
| `~/.claude.json` | MCP servers (user + per-project), app state, UI toggles — **not** where `permissions`/`hooks`/`env` go | User |
| Managed policy file (`/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md` on macOS, `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md` on Linux/WSL, `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md` on Windows) | Org-wide instructions from IT/DevOps | Org |

Directories added with `--add-dir`/`/add-dir` load skills (live reload) and subagents from that directory, plus only the `enabledPlugins`/`extraKnownMarketplaces` settings keys; CLAUDE.md/rules there load only with `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1`. Directories listed under `permissions.additionalDirectories` grant file access only — no configuration is discovered from them. Hooks and other `settings.json` keys load only from the current working directory's `.claude/` plus `~/.claude/settings.json` and managed settings — no parent-directory fallback (an exception: `.claude/settings.local.json` loads from the git repo root as of v2.1.211).

## CLAUDE.md vs auto memory

| | CLAUDE.md files | Auto memory (`MEMORY.md`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who writes it | You | Claude |
| Contains | Instructions and rules | Learnings and patterns Claude discovered |
| Scope | Project, user, or org | Per repository, shared across worktrees |
| Loaded into | Every session, in full regardless of length | Every session, first 200 lines or 25KB only |
| Use for | Coding standards, workflows, architecture | Build commands, debugging insights, preferences |

Both are delivered as context (a user message after the system prompt), not enforced configuration — Claude tries to follow them but compliance isn't guaranteed, especially for vague/conflicting instructions. Anything that must run at a fixed point (before every commit, after each edit) belongs in a **hook**, not CLAUDE.md. CLAUDE.md files load in load order from broadest to most specific scope (managed policy → user `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` → project → local), so project instructions appear in context after user instructions. Subdirectory `CLAUDE.md` files load on demand when Claude Reads a file in that directory, not at session start.

`MEMORY.md` lives under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`; when it nears the 200-line/25KB limit Claude Code reminds Claude to shorten it, and a write that exceeds the limit still succeeds but everything past the limit is silently dropped on next load. Detail should move into topic files (`debugging.md`, `patterns.md`) that Claude reads on demand — those are not auto-loaded at startup. A subagent's own conversation doesn't inherit the main session's auto memory (except a fork, which inherits everything); a subagent can have its own separate memory directory via its `memory` field.

## Settings files and precedence

Precedence, **highest to lowest** (each level overrides the one below for a given key; arrays generally concatenate rather than override):

1. **Managed settings** — server-managed / MDM / `managed-settings.json` — cannot be overridden by anything, including CLI flags
2. **Command-line arguments** (`--settings <file-or-json>`)
3. **Local project settings** (`.claude/settings.local.json`) — personal, gitignored
4. **Shared project settings** (`.claude/settings.json`) — team-shared, committed
5. **User settings** (`~/.claude/settings.json`) — personal, global

Key `settings.json` blocks: `permissions` (allow/deny/ask rules, `defaultMode`, `additionalDirectories`), `hooks` (scripts on lifecycle events, matched by tool name), `env` (session-wide environment variables), `statusLine`, `model`, `enabledPlugins`/`pluginConfigs`/`extraKnownMarketplaces` (plugin config), `autoMode` (see below). `~/.claude.json` is a different file from `~/.claude/settings.json` — MCP/app-state vs. permissions/hooks/env respectively; putting `permissions`/`hooks`/`env` in `~/.claude.json` is silently ignored.

`.claude/settings.local.json`'s allow rule

summary_cases.body_excerpt:
# BUG-205 — Sync Customer Schemas workflow fails provisioning Ad-Hoc pipeline group (uuid NOT NULL)

The nightly `Sync Customer Schemas` GitHub Actions workflow dies with a Postgres NotNullViolation when it tries to create the `Ad-Hoc` pipeline group for a newly-provisioned customer schema.

---

# Problem

The scheduled `Sync Customer Schemas` workflow (`.github/workflows/sync_customer_schemas.yaml`, `on: schedule`) failed on run #788 (2026-07-16 02:47 UTC, commit `18ae74e`). It had been green through 2026-07-15, so this is the first failure. The `run-script` job exits with code 1 on:

```text
sqlalchemy.exc.IntegrityError: (psycopg2.errors.NotNullViolation) null value in column "uuid" of relation "pipeline_groups" violates not-null constraint
DETAIL:  Failing row contains (1, Ad-Hoc, 2026-07-16 02:48:13.194451, null, 4, null, null).
[SQL:
    INSERT INTO notslog.pipeline_groups (name, created_by, created_at)
    VALUES ('Ad-Hoc', 4, now())
    RETURNING id
]
```

Impact: the sync run aborts entirely, so any customer schema that still needs provisioning does not get created/synced until the bug is fixed.

# Root Cause

Migration `api/alembic/versions/a1b2c3d4e5f6_add_uuid_to_pipeline_groups.py` (landed in commit `c6be468f6`, "Add UUID to pipeline groups and support group export/import") adds `pipeline_groups.uuid VARCHAR NOT NULL` with **no server default**:

```sql
ALTER TABLE "{schema}".pipeline_groups ADD COLUMN uuid VARCHAR;
UPDATE "{schema}".pipeline_groups SET uuid = gen_random_uuid()::text WHERE uuid IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE "{schema}".pipeline_groups ALTER COLUMN uuid SET NOT NULL;
```

The raw ad-hoc provisioning INSERT in `api/sync_customer_schemas.py:118` was not updated alongside the migration — it omits the `uuid` column, so the NOT NULL constraint fires. The companion migration `api/alembic/versions/provision_universal_adhoc_loss_run.py:59` *was* updated (it supplies `gen_random_uuid()::text`), which is why the gap went unnoticed until the scheduled sync hit a schema (`notslog`) needing a fresh Ad-Hoc group.

# Investigation Notes

- 2026-07-16 — Confirmed via `gh run view 29467421718 --log-failed`: single failing site is the Ad-Hoc `pipeline_groups` INSERT. `Generate Ad Hoc Claims Data` workflow (the other scheduled "adhoc" job) is unrelated and green (see BUG-206 for its separate data-flow issue).
- Verified `grep -rn "INSERT INTO.*pipeline_groups"` across `*.py`: only two insert sites — the fixed migration and `sync_customer_schemas.py`. No other uuid-less inserts remain after the fix.
- The `actions/checkout@v3` Node 20 deprecation warning in the same run is unrelated noise, not the failure.
- 2026-07-16 — Fix committed on worktree branch `BUG-205-adhoc-pipeline-group-uuid` (`5e1461a7a`); status → `fix-ready`. Pushed and opened as [PR #1093](https://github.com/aclaimant/data-pipline-dashboard/pull/1093).
- 2026-07-21 — Linked to ClickUp [OWL-19836](https://app.clickup.com/t/10537780/OWL-19836) "Fix for Ad-Hoc pipeline Group Creation".
- 2026-07-24 — PR #1093 merged by Nathan Whyte (`42f6930e`). Status → `fixed`.
- 2026-07-16 — **Git archaeology (how the gap arose).** The runtime Ad-Hoc INSERT in `sync_customer_schemas.py` was introduced by Jerrvon Ewing in `e875abe70` (2026-04-01, "Provision adhoc loss run…") and **never contained `uuid`** — `git log -S "pipeline_groups (name, created_by, created_at, uuid"` confirms the only commit that has ever added `uuid` to this INSERT is the fix (`5e1461a7a`). The `pipeline_groups.uuid` column itself was added by Joel Friedman (`c6be468f6`, 2026-03-23) and hardened to `NOT NULL` + backfilled by Nathan Whyte (`bde15547e` "patch pipeline group UUID revision for more safeguards", `ed5347655` "Add additional backfill for pipeline group UUIDs", both 2026-04-08). Notably the **sibling** migration INSERT in `provision_universal_adhoc_loss_run.py` *was* updated for the same constraint by Jerrvon (`f795cc33b`, 2026-04-10, "Fix non null constraint" — supplies `gen_random_uuid()::text`), but the equivalent **runtime** provisioning INSERT in `sync_customer_schemas.py` was missed. So the NOT-NULL hardening (correct) simply outran the one runtime write-path that was never brought into line — the gap sat latent until the 2026-07-16 sync hit a schema needing a fresh Ad-Hoc group.

# Fix

Add the `uuid` column to the raw INSERT, mirroring the migration:

```sql
INSERT INTO {slug}.pipeline_groups (name, created_by, created_at, uuid)
VALUES ('Ad-Hoc', 4, now(), gen_random_uuid()::text)
RETURNING id
```

Committed to branch `BUG-205-adhoc-pipeline-group-uuid` (off `origin/main` @ `18ae74ef1`) as `5e1461a7a` — a minimal 2-line change to `api/sync_customer_schemas.py:118-119`. Pushed and opened as [PR #1093](https://github.com/aclaimant/data-pipline-dashboard/pull/1093). (Deliberately skipped the full `ruff format` pass: `origin/main`'s copy of the file is unformatted, so formatting would add ~130 lines of unrelated churn — any format pass should be its own commit.)

# Verification

Merged as `42f6930e` on 2026-07-24. The `Sync Customer Schemas` workflow should be re-run against a schema needing a fresh Ad-Hoc group to confirm the fix at runtime; the nightly cron run will pick it up automatically.

# IMPR-1008 — Complete OpenViking v0.4.4 multi-tenant auth migration

_Finish migrating consumers from root API key to user-scoped API key after upgrading OV to v0.4.4 in commit `2ea4c57`. The image upgrade is live; consumer migration is partial — `compendium-sync.py` works (env-pass pattern compatible), but Hermes deployment env and several docs/examples still reference the root key._

---

# Status update (2026-06-23)

**The data-API access gap is resolved — via trusted mode, not user keys.** See [[BUG-1022-homelab-ov-trusted-mode-tenant-data-auth]] (commit `71322a3`). Investigation during FEAT-1017 intake showed the premise below — that a user/admin key works for tenant data in v0.4.4 — does **not** hold: v0.4.4's `ApiKeyAuthPlugin` rejects root (`PERMISSION_DENIED`) _and_ returns `UNAUTHENTICATED "Invalid API Key"` for user/admin keys (both roles, every header form), so no key reaches tenant data in `api_key` mode. The server's own error message names the working path ("…or trusted mode for upstream identity assertion"). `server.auth_mode = "trusted"` was set live: the root key is still required (host `0.0.0.0`, enforced by `trusted.py`) but `X-OpenViking-Account`/`X-OpenViking-User` headers are trusted, restoring the root-key + identity-headers pattern compendium-sync, the OV MCP, and Hermes' OV tools already use. Verified: compendium-sync 4/4 ok, `ov ls` rc=0, HTTP search 200, and the BUG-1021 self-bootstrap 403 noise stopped.

**What remains in scope here** is now the _hardening_ layer, not the unblock: the two-key Secret shape, `ov-rotate-user-key.sh`, consumer docs, and the `ovcli.conf` recipe are still worth doing **if/when a future OV build validates user/admin keys for data APIs** — at which point `auth_mode` can revert to `api_key` and trusted mode can retire. Until then, trusted mode is the steady state and the "user key for data" steps below are deferred (the user key does not authenticate for data in v0.4.4). Priority reduced accordingly.

# Status update (2026-07-04)

**The re-test trigger is here: v0.4.7 is staged** ([[IMPR-1032-homelab-openviking-v047-upgrade-native-observability|IMPR-1032]], homelab branch `impr-1032-ov-v047-upgrade`). Two v0.4.5–v0.4.7 changes bear directly on this entry: v0.4.5 fixed the trusted-mode Role serialization (the fix upstream explicitly recommends for our deployment shape), and **v0.4.7 adds seeded API key generation** to auth. After the IMPR-1032 Phase B rollout, re-run the BUG-1022 key-validation matrix (user/admin key vs tenant data APIs in `api_key` mode) on v0.4.7 — if keys now validate, the deferred hardening steps below un-defer and `auth_mode` can revert from `trusted`.

---

# Current Behavior

OV v0.4.4 introduces a multi-tenant auth model that **rejects root API keys for tenant-scoped data APIs** with `PERMISSION_DENIED — ROOT API keys cannot access tenant-scoped data APIs in api_key mode`. The root key now only works for `ov admin` subcommands (with `--sudo`) and a few status endpoints. All data operations (`mkdir`, `add-resource`, `ls`, `find`, etc.) require a user-scoped key.

summary_cases.body_excerpt:
# IDEA-023 — Consolidate Redundant Agent Documentation and Local HTTP Proxy for MCP Debugging

_Pattern for keeping agent docs lean by removing CLI syntax references (which `--help` covers) and a method for debugging MCP parameter forwarding using a local HTTP request proxy._

---

# Idea

## Documentation Consolidation

Agent documentation (CLAUDE.md, OPENVIKING.md, etc.) naturally accumulates references to CLI flag docs, subcommand lists, and syntax tables. These are expensive in token context and duplicative of built-in help (`cmd --help`). The pattern is:

1. Identify standalone CLI syntax reference files that duplicate `--help` output
2. Delete them (they're always stale, and `cmd --help` is authoritative)
3. Update cross-references to point to `--help` instead of the deleted file
4. Keep strategy/mechanics/guide docs separate from CLAUDE.md to avoid bloat (see OPENVIKING.md staying separate)

## MCP Parameter Debugging via Local HTTP Proxy

When an MCP tool passes parameters but the downstream API ignores them, the root cause is often a mismatch between the JSON body field name the API expects and what the MCP server sends. The fastest way to discover the correct field name is to proxy a CLI tool (which works correctly) through a local HTTP server:

1. Start a Python HTTP server on a local port that logs request bodies:

   ```python
   python3 -c "from http.server import HTTPServer, BaseHTTPRequestHandler; ...
   ```

2. Point the working CLI at the proxy (e.g., via env vars or `--api-url`)
3. Capture the exact JSON body the CLI sends
4. Compare to what the MCP server sends — the field names will differ
5. Fix the MCP server to match the CLI's field names

This is faster than guessing field names, reading API docs, or adding debug prints to the MCP server (which requires restarting the MCP runtime).

# Open Questions

- Could the MCP server auto-learn API field names from an OpenAPI spec?
- Should CLI syntax reference be auto-generated from `--help` output instead of manually maintained?

summary_cases.body_excerpt:
# INFO-092 — OpenViking vs Mem0 Comparison

_Head-to-head comparison of the two leading candidates for the DipDash KB context/memory layer. OpenViking is the current homelab choice; Mem0 is the leading production alternative. Evaluates architecture, features, trade-offs, and a hybrid option._

---

# At a Glance

| | OpenViking | Mem0 |
|---|---|---|
| **What it is** | Context database for AI agents | Memory platform for AI agents |
| **Creator** | ByteDance (Volcano Engine) | Mem0 (YC W24, $24M Series A) |
| **GitHub stars** | ~15K | 47.8K |
| **Current version** | v0.3.x | v0.1.x (OSS) / managed cloud |
| **License** | Apache 2.0 | MIT (OSS) / proprietary (cloud) |
| **Core metaphor** | Filesystem (`viking://` URIs) | Memory extraction + retrieval |
| **Best for** | Structured, hierarchical content | Conversational, operational memory |

---

# Architecture Comparison

## OpenViking: Filesystem Paradigm

Content is organized as a URI-addressed filesystem with three root directories:

```yaml
viking://resources/  — raw data (PDFs, code, specs, docs)
viking://user/       — user-specific info (preferences, history)
viking://agent/      — agent skills and operational experience
```

Every piece of content is processed into three levels on write:

- **L0 (Abstract):** <100 tokens — quick relevance check
- **L1 (Overview):** ~2K tokens — planning decisions
- **L2 (Full):** Complete content — deep reads on demand

Retrieval uses **directory-recursive search**: vector search identifies the relevant directory, then the agent navigates within it using semantic search + glob/grep. This preserves hierarchy and context — the opposite of "vector soup."

## Mem0: Memory Extraction Platform

Content is ingested via `add()` calls (or auto-extracted from conversations). The platform:

1. **Extracts** facts, preferences, and relationships from text automatically
2. **Deduplicates** — avoids storing the same fact twice
3. **Resolves conflicts** — when new info contradicts old, resolves it
4. **Stores** in hybrid backend — vector (all tiers) + graph (Pro tier) + key-value
5. **Retrieves** via `search()` with user/agent scoping

No filesystem, no hierarchy, no tiered loading. Memories are flat entities with metadata and (on Pro) graph relationships.

---

# Feature-by-Feature

## Where OpenViking Wins

| Feature | Why it matters for IDEA-040 |
|---|---|
| **Filesystem paradigm** | Maps directly to a taxonomy-based KB. Content is organized by domain/theme/tag in directories, just like compendium. Agents navigate predictably. |
| **Tiered loading (L0/L1/L2)** | Critical for a ~1.75M-token corpus. Agents skim L0, plan at L1, deep-read L2 — saves >80% tokens vs loading full content. Mem0 has no equivalent. |
| **Directory-recursive retrieval** | Avoids "vector soup" — returns structured results with hierarchical context, not disconnected chunks. IDEA-040 explicitly identifies this as a key problem. |
| **Author-controlled content** | You define the files, frontmatter, and directory structure. OV indexes what you give it. Mem0 auto-extracts — you get what the ML decides is a "fact." |
| **URI-based addressing** | Every entry has a stable URI (`viking://resources/compendium/bugs/bug-042.md`). Enables citation, cross-reference, dedup. |
| **Append-only audit log** | Fits the compendium model (log = SOT, indexed content = rebuildable read model). Mem0 doesn't have an audit log concept. |
| **No per-query cost** | Self-hosted, GPU-accelerated embedding. No per-memory pricing. |
| **Already deployed** | Running in K3s, compendium-sync wired up, pain points documented. Zero migration cost for homelab phase. |

## Where Mem0 Wins

| Feature | Why it matters for IDEA-040 |
|---|---|
| **Auto-extraction** | No need to manually structure content as files with frontmatter. Conversations, Slack messages, and unstructured docs can be ingested as-is. OV requires pre-structured input. |
| **Multi-user/agent scoping** | Built-in user isolation. For a 30-person team, this is essential. OV has scopes (personal/compendium) but not user-level permissions. |
| **Dedup + conflict resolution** | When the same fact appears in multiple sources (Slack + Notion + compendium), Mem0 deduplicates and resolves conflicts automatically. OV indexes each file independently — no cross-source dedup. |
| **Graph memory (Pro)** | Entity relationships extracted automatically. "This API depends on that service" — the kind of relational knowledge OV's hierarchy doesn't capture well. |
| **Managed option** | Zero ops. For production AWS deployment, this eliminates running your own context database, monitoring, backups, upgrades. OV on AWS = you run everything. |
| **Community + maturity** | 47.8K stars vs 15K. More tutorials, integrations, and battle-testing. YC-backed company with funding. OV is ByteDance OSS with less transparent roadmap. |
| **Conflict resolution** | When a fact changes ("API moved from /v1 to /v2"), Mem0 updates it. OV requires a file update + re-sync. |

## Where Both Are Equal

| Feature | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Self-hostable** | Both can run on K8s. OV is lighter (single service + embedder). Mem0 needs Postgres + (optionally) Neo4j for graph. |
| **API simplicity** | Both have minimal APIs. OV: `add`, `search`, `read`, `ls`. Mem0: `add`, `search`, `get`, `delete`. |
| **Framework agnostic** | Both work with any LLM/agent framework. OV has native OpenClaw integration but a generic API. Mem0 has LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations but is framework-agnostic. |

---

# Pain Point Mapping

Known OV pain points from PROJ-027 exploration, and how Mem0 would handle them:

| # | OV Pain Point | Mem0 Status |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Negative queries return garbage (0.44 floor) | **Better** — Mem0 can return empty results when no relevant memories found, rather than forcing results |
| P2 | Exact-ID queries are weak | **Different** — Mem0 doesn't have IDs at all; it's entity/fact-based. Would need a separate lookup layer (same as IDEA-046) |
| P3

summary_cases.body_excerpt:
# IDEA-013 — Migrate away from Mage Orchestration

_Evaluate replacing Mage as the pipeline orchestrator, preserving the dbt/Snowflake data layer, DipDash status tracking, and ECS infrastructure._

---

# Idea

Mage is the current pipeline orchestrator for 40 customer ingestion pipelines (36 production, 4 test/dev). It provides DAG execution, a web UI, run tracking, and inter-pipeline triggering. The business logic (dbt models, Snowflake exports, DipDash notifications, S3 loaders, Soda data quality) is largely framework-agnostic and could run under any orchestrator. The Mage coupling is a thin but pervasive layer of decorators, SDK calls, and `metadata.yaml` DAG definitions that would need rewriting.

A feasibility research document (`docs/research/2026-04-27-mage-migration-feasibility.md`) mapped the full coupling surface:

- **40 pipelines** (36 production, 4 test/dev) defined via Mage `metadata.yaml` DAG schemas — two patterns: 1 data-driven pipeline (config-driven, serves many customers) and 30+ per-customer template pipelines
- **15,577 Python LOC** total; **8,048 (52%) Mage-coupled**, 7,331 (47%) framework-agnostic
- **70+ blocks** using `@data_loader` / `@data_exporter` / `@transformer` / `@sensor` / `@callback` / `@custom` decorators
- **Key Mage SDK calls**: `trigger_pipeline()` (inter-pipeline orchestration), `check_status()` (status polling), `Snowflake.with_config()`, `S3.with_config()`, `get_secret_value()`, `ConfigFileLoader`/`AWSSecretLoader`
- **DipDash HTTP POST is the sole trigger** — no cron schedules, no S3 events, no Mage-native triggers
- **Column mappings flow is structurally Mage-coupled** — DipDash → Mage exporter → Snowflake → dbt compile-time queries; per-run schema naming and execution ordering are coordinated by Mage's DAG model
- **Soda data quality** is double-coupled — `@transformer` decorators + `ConfigFileLoader` for Snowflake credentials; but `soda-core` library and 9 check configs + 7 customer overrides are portable
- **dbt layer is fully portable** — 1,321 SQL files run via `dbt run`, not Mage
- **DipDash stage tracking is decoupled** — REST API calls, no Mage internals
- **AWS ECS infrastructure is reusable** — Terraform-provisioned cluster, RDS, S3, ALB, IAM roles
- **Estimated effort: 5–8 engineer-weeks** for production-ready migration

**Orchestrator candidates** (from comparison matrix): **Prefect** is the closest drop-in (decorator style mirrors Mage, medium rewrite). **Dagster** is the best architectural upgrade (asset-based dbt lineage). **Airflow/MWAA** is the safest enterprise bet.

**Key risks**: Parallel-run is **unsafe** without DipDash changes (schema collision, `pipeline_run_info` state corruption). Shadow-mode (new orchestrator runs without DipDash writeback) is the only safe parallel strategy. The fail sensor (`PipelineRun`/`BlockRun` ORM) is completely non-portable and must be fully rewritten.

This idea explores whether replacing Mage is a better investment than FEAT-015 (running Mage on ECS executor). The two approaches share infrastructure work but differ in scope: FEAT-015 keeps Mage as orchestrator, this idea replaces it entirely.

# Open Questions

## Answered by Gap Review (2026-04-27)

- ~~What orchestrator would replace Mage?~~ → See comparison matrix in research doc: Prefect (closest drop-in), Dagster (best upgrade), Airflow (safest enterprise)
- ~~How many of the 39 pipelines are active vs. deprecated?~~ → 40 total: 36 production, 4 test/dev fixtures (`ecs_test_pipeline`, `mikestc_testing_lr_ingestion`, `fail_sensor`, `skip_stage`)
- ~~How does this relate to FEAT-015?~~ → Complementary; FEAT-015 can be a stepping stone (shared ECS infra work)

## Remaining

- What replaces the Mage web UI for monitoring and manual triggering? (DipDash handles triggering; monitoring is the gap)
- How tightly is DipDash's frontend tied to Mage run IDs and block structure beyond the trigger API?
- Should dbt run standalone (dbt Cloud / dbt Core CLI) or via the new orchestrator?
- What replaces `@test` decorator and test-mode pipelines?
- What's the acceptable migration window? Data-driven pipeline first, then batch-migrate template pipelines?
- Does the Fivetran integration (`refresh_fivetran.py`) need orchestrator-native hooks?
- Should migration include Snowflake orphan schema cleanup? (per-run schemas are never cleaned up today)
- Is DipDash backend work in scope? (parallel-run requires DipDash changes for separate `schema_suffix` namespaces)

# Related

- [[FEAT-015-mage-switch-mage-ecs-executor|FEAT-015]] — Switch Mage to ECS executor (complementary — same AWS infra, different scope)
- IDEA-1002 — Document Mage-to-Snowflake data export path (cross-reference)
- [[PROJ-007-mage-performance-concurrency-isolation|PROJ-007]] — Original performance concern motivating this evaluation

# BUG-185 — SET_TO_BLANK on custom (business) validations has no effect on field values used in matching

_The custom validation UI exposes `SET_TO_BLANK` as an error-level option on business validations, but it is silently ignored when that field is also read by the matching CTE._

---

# Problem

The custom validation UI lets users configure `SET_TO_BLANK` as an error level on business (custom) validations. Users configuring this expect the flagged field's value to be blanked wherever it's used — including in claim/policy matching.

In practice, `SET_TO_BLANK` is only applied to field values in `pre_stg_standard_format_validated`, which reads exclusively from `asf_INTRINSIC_validations`. Business (custom) validations are never read there. Business validations are only read in the matching CTE to filter rows by `SUSPEND_ROW` or `FAIL_PIPELINE` — there is no code path that applies `SET_TO_BLANK` from a business validation to the value used in matching.

Net effect: a user sets `SET_TO_BLANK` on a business validation expecting it to blank the field, but the un-blanked value still flows into matching, potentially producing incorrect match results.

# Discovery

Found while investigating a fuzzy match conflict on claim `P 22023565001` (Doherty Liberty Risktrac).

# Root Cause (preliminary)

Two independent read paths exist for validation error levels:

1. `asf_INTRINSIC_validations` → `pre_stg_standard_format_validated` — this path honors `SET_TO_BLANK`.
2. Business (custom) validations → matching CTE — this path only checks for `SUSPEND_ROW` / `FAIL_PIPELINE`; `SET_TO_BLANK` has no effect here.

Needs further investigation to confirm exact model/file locations in both dipdash (validation UI / config) and mage (matching CTE, dbt models).

# Verification

- [ ] Confirm root cause with a reproduction on a business validation configured with SET_TO_BLANK on a matching-relevant field
- [ ] Decide fix: either apply SET_TO_BLANK to the value read by the matching CTE, or remove SET_TO_BLANK as a valid option for business validations if it can't apply there

heading-anchored classifier missed cards written as `##` or with no heading.

# Current Behavior

Task Board is now the selected board plugin for the personal notes/task operating system, but the live configuration and task corpus are still too broad and internally inconsistent:

- `.obsidian/plugins/task-board/data.json` defines a "Tag Based Workflow" with active `namedTag` columns for `task/status/inbox`, `task/status/next`, `task/status/doing`, `task/status/waiting`, and `task/status/someday`, plus a checkbox-driven `completed` column.
- The plugin cache in `.obsidian/plugins/task-board/tasks.json` contains 4,709 cached task cards: 3,398 pending and 1,311 completed.
- A source scan found 4,806 Markdown checkbox lines across the vault, but only 17 lines with `#task/status/*` tags. Most cached cards come from acceptance criteria, plans, docs, templates, and historical project checklists rather than intentional board cards.
- The current scan filters in Task Board are empty, and `showTaskWithoutMetadata` is enabled, so untagged checklist items become board cards.
- Some completed inbox items still carry active status tags such as `#task/status/inbox`, which makes completion semantics ambiguous.
- QuickAdd currently writes captured tasks to both `notes/inbox.md` and `notes/today.md`, which can create duplicate board cards.
- Documentation and agent instructions originally described `#task/status/*` integration without clearly separating board-card tags from compendium entry lifecycle frontmatter or acceptance-criteria checkboxes; the 2026-06-29 documentation pass has updated the main related entries, but live task/config cleanup remains.

# Proposed Improvement

Standardize Task Board as an explicit board-card surface, not a whole-vault checklist viewer.

Acceptance criteria:

1. Define the canonical board statuses as exactly one active tag per live board task:
   - `#task/status/inbox`
   - `#task/status/next`
   - `#task/status/doing`
   - `#task/status/waiting`
   - `#task/status/someday`
2. Treat completion as primarily checkbox state (`- [x]`) because the active Task Board config uses a checkbox-based Completed column. If `#task/status/done` remains useful for search/history, ensure completed tasks do not also retain any active live-state tag.
3. Update compendium TASK conventions so each visible TASK entry has at most one dedicated board-card checkbox, while acceptance criteria remain untagged checkboxes.
4. Update QuickAdd so captured task cards have one canonical source of truth, preferably `notes/inbox.md`; `notes/today.md` should plan/reference work rather than duplicate inbox cards.
5. Configure Task Board scan or board filters so the primary board excludes non-action checklist sources such as `docs/`, `_scripts/`, `.claude/`, `_sources/`, `.stversions/`, `plans/`, templates, completed/resolved/archive folders, and other historical/checklist-heavy areas.
6. Clean current inconsistent status tags, including checked tasks that still carry active tags.
7. Keep `GUIDE-1063`, `TASK-1085`, `PROJ-1011`, `IDEA-1046`, `INFO-1067`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `.claude/instructions/tasks.md` consistent with the final board-card convention.
8. Add a lightweight hygiene check that flags:
   - checked tasks with active `#task/status/inbox|next|doing|waiting|someday` tags
   - unchecked tasks tagged `#task/status/done`
   - multiple `#task/status/*` tags on one line
   - live board tags inside documentation/example checklists
   - compendium TASK entries with zero or multiple dedicated board-card lines

# Impact

This should make Task Board usable as the day-to-day execution surface instead of a noisy mirror of every Markdown checklist in the vault. Expected outcomes:

- Board card count drops from thousands of accidental checklist cards to the small set of intentional live work items.
- Completion semantics become obvious: active work is tagged, completed work is checked off.
- Compendium TASK files can still appear on the board without polluting it with every acceptance criterion.
- QuickAdd capture becomes less duplicative and easier to reason about.
- Future agents have concrete rules for adding board-visible tasks without reintroducing scan noise.

# BUG-199 — ACCO Liberty Claims pipeline config save blocked by stale asf_model value

Saving the ACCO Liberty Claims pipeline configuration fails with a 400 error referencing an asf_model template that does not exist.

---

# Problem

Users cannot save any changes to the ACCO Liberty Claims pipeline configuration (`acco_liberty_risktrac_dynamic_ingestion`) via the DipDash pipeline settings UI. Every `PATCH /configuration` request returns:

```text
400: No template found with source_name 'liberty_risktrac_dynamic'. asf_model must reference an existing template in column mappings, table joins, or lookups.
```

This surfaced when Sean Tognetti attempted Joel Friedman's suggested workaround for BUG-195 (toggle `fail_unmatched_claims` to `false`, save, then toggle back to `true`) — the intermediate save failed with this error instead of persisting.

# Root Cause

In `api/app/api_v1/endpoints/customer_level/pipeline_level/configuration.py`, `validate_asf_model()` (lines 92-107) checks that `merged_config["asf_model"]` matches an existing `source_name` in `ColumnMappingCommon`, `TableJoinCommon`, or `LookupCommon`. `update_configuration()` (lines 126-180) merges the existing DB config with the incoming request body (`merged_config = {**existing_config, **filtered_incoming}`, line 162) and runs this validation whenever `"asf_model"` or `"stage_2_type"` is present anywhere in the incoming request (line 166) — not only when `asf_model` is actually being changed.

Two things combine to trip this on saves unrelated to `asf_model`:

1. The DipDash frontend defensively resubmits the entire pipeline config on every save (a known compensating pattern for an older full-replace/silent-data-loss bug — see prior session observations #1481/#1497, 2026-05-20), so `asf_model` is present in essentially every PATCH request body regardless of what the user is actually editing.
2. This pipeline's stored `asf_model` value is `liberty_risktrac_dynamic`, which does not match any registered template. Confirmed via a direct dev DB query: `common.column_mappings` only has `source_name = 'liberty_risktrac'` (no `_dynamic` suffix). The stale value likely originated from confusion with the pipeline's own path name (`acco_liberty_risktrac_dynamic_ingestion`) during an earlier config save, before merged-config validation was enforced.

The validation logic itself is correct and was tightened as part of a Jul 8 fix (session observation #14242, same file) that stopped a prior bug where partial saves would silently drop unlisted config fields (matching the general full-replace/data-loss pattern in obs #1481). That fix now properly validates the persisted merged config — which is why a previously-tolerated bad `asf_model` value is now blocking saves it previously wouldn't have caught.

Whether the validation should be scoped so it only runs when `asf_model` is actually _changing_ to a new value (vs. merely present in a full-form resubmission) is a candidate follow-up — see Fix options below.

# Investigation Notes

- 2026-07-15: Traced from a Slack thread (Sean Tognetti / Joel Friedman, #C08Q7S22NGG) — user hit this error trying to save `fail_unmatched_claims=false` as an intermediate step in the BUG-195 toggle workaround.
- Ran the `error-diagnostic` skill: `viking_grep` for the exact error text and for "asf_model must reference" returned 0 matches in the compendium vault — this is a new error signature, not previously filed.
- Confirmed root cause by reading `api/app/api_v1/endpoints/customer_level/pipeline_level/configuration.py:92-180` and querying the dev DB directly: `common.column_mappings` has `source_name='liberty_risktrac'` (49+ rows returned), no row for `liberty_risktrac_dynamic` in `column_mappings`, `table_joins`, or `lookups`.
- 2026-07-15: Queried **prod** directly (dev diverges here — dev's copy of the Claims pipeline already has the correct `asf_model`). Prod has the stale value on **two** pipelines, not one: `acco_liberty_risktrac_dynamic_ingestion` and `acco_liberty_risktrac_dynamic_policy_ingestion` both have `asf_model = 'liberty_risktrac_dynamic'`. Confirmed `liberty_risktrac` is the only Liberty-related template in prod's `common.column_mappings`/`table_joins`/`lookups`, and no other prod pipeline (within `acco`) has a similarly-mismatched `asf_model`.
- 2026-07-15: Implementation plan written — [[2026-07-15-BUG-199-asf-model-validation-scope-fix]] (`docs/plans/`). Fix scoped into two parts: a code change (validate `asf_model` existence only when its value changes) and a one-off prod data correction, kept separate per decision below.

# Fix

Two parts, scoped separately per plan decision (code fix ships via PR; data fix is a manual step run against prod after review — not bundled into the same deploy):

1. **Prod data correction**: guarded, idempotent `UPDATE ... jsonb_set` correcting `asf_model` from `liberty_risktrac_dynamic` to `liberty_risktrac` for both `acco_liberty_risktrac_dynamic_ingestion` and `acco_liberty_risktrac_dynamic_policy_ingestion`. Script: `_sources/2026-07/2026-07-15_bug-199-fix-acco-liberty-asf-model.sql`. Run manually against prod only (dev's Claims-pipeline copy is already correct).
2. **Code fix**: scope `validate_asf_model()`'s existence check to only fire when `asf_model`'s value is actually changing (diff `existing_config.get("asf_model")` vs. the incoming value), and split the compatibility check so it degrades gracefully when the stored `asf_model` doesn't resolve to any template. # IMPR-1079 — Guide capable agents to choose parallel subagents for parallelizable flows

Add behavioral guidance so hosted/capable agents consistently recognize parallelizable flows and
fan out subagents to multi-task, instead of grinding serially or deferring to a single subagent and
idling.

---

# Current Behavior

There is guidance telling **local-model** agents to _avoid_ parallel subagents (IMPR-1066 — MLX
serializes, so fan-out is pure loss), but **no positive counterpart** telling **capable (hosted
Claude)** agents to actively parallelize when a flow supports it. As a result:

- Agents default to serial work even when subtasks are independent (multi-file research, per-item
  vault edits, review across dimensions), leaving wall-clock speedup on the table.
- A recurring failure mode: an agent dispatches **one** subagent and then idles, waiting — a ~50%
  throughput loss for a task that either needed no subagent or wanted several.
- The infrastructure to do this well now exists — the `/bg` family and custom `bg-*` agents
  (IMPR-1072), the `Workflow` orchestration patterns, and the bulk-edit subagent pattern
  (GUIDE-021 A7) — but the **decision of when to fan out is ad-hoc**, so it happens inconsistently.

# Proposed Improvement

Add agent-instruction guidance (a behavioral rule in the dotfiles `CLAUDE.md` / agent config,
complementing IMPR-1066's `local-model-append.md` but for the capable-session case) that codifies:

1. **A catalog of parallelizable flow patterns** worth fanning out — e.g. independent multi-file
   research/search sweeps, per-item vault edits (bulk frontmatter, multi-item intake), review
   across independent dimensions (correctness / perf / security), and multi-source investigation.
   These are the shapes the `bg-*` agents and `Workflow` patterns already target.
2. **A fan-out-vs-serial heuristic**: parallelize when subtasks are **independent** (no shared
   mutable state, no ordering dependency) and each is **substantial enough** to amortize spawn cost;
   stay serial for trivial or dependent work. Never dispatch one subagent and idle — either do it
   inline or fan out ≥2.
3. **Capability gating.** This applies to hosted Claude sessions and is the **inverse** of IMPR-1066
   for local models. Ideally keyed on the same runtime signal as IMPR-1073 (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`),
   so parallel-encourage auto-enables on hosted sessions and parallel-avoid on local ones — one
   detection, two opposite policies.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- Guidance exists in agent instructions naming concrete parallelizable flow patterns and the
  fan-out-vs-serial heuristic, and explicitly cross-references IMPR-1066 for the local-model case.
- It is gated to capable (non-local) sessions.
- Observable effect: given an independent multi-lane task, a capable session dispatches parallel
  subagents rather than working serially or deferring to a single idle subagent.

# Impact

Faster multi-tasking on capable sessions, and — paired with IMPR-1066 — a complete, capability-aware
policy: **parallelize when it helps, don't when it doesn't**, decided by session type rather than by
each agent guessing. Directly targets the dispatch-one-and-idle waste.

# Related

- Avoid-side counterpart (local models): [[IMPR-1066-dotfiles-local-model-agents-should-avoid-parallel-subagents|IMPR-1066 Local-model agents should avoid parallel subagents]]
- The flows this parallelizes: [[IMPR-1072-other-bg-background-subagent-slash-command-family|IMPR-1072 /bg background-subagent slash command family]]
- Shared capability gate: [[IMPR-1073-other-runtime-local-model-detection-via-anthropic-base-url-to-auto|IMPR-1073 runtime local-model detection]]
- Bulk-edit subagent pattern: GUIDE-021 A7 (compendium authoring standard)

# Sources

- Conversation, 2026-07-17 — arose while building the `/bg` command family and custom `bg-*` agents;
  the need for consistent fan-out on capable sessions (vs. IMPR-1066's local-model avoidance) surfaced
  as the missing encourage-side policy.

# BUG-1076 — equal-risk-pdb selector matches no pods, so equal-risk-rails is unprotected during drains

_A PodDisruptionBudget whose selector matches nothing reports `disruptionsAllowed: 0`, which looks like maximum protection and actually means it governs no pods at all._

---

# Problem

`equal-risk/equal-risk-pdb` is declared `minAvailable: 1` over selector `app=rails`. No pod carries that label — the running pod is `equal-risk-rails-*`, labeled `app=equal-risk-rails` — so the PDB covers zero pods and constrains nothing during eviction.

Live state, captured 2026-08-07:

```text
spec.selector.matchLabels   {"app": "rails"}
spec.minAvailable           1
status.expectedPods         0
status.currentHealthy       0
status.desiredHealthy       1
status.disruptionsAllowed   0
```

The misleading part is `disruptionsAllowed: 0`. Read casually — including in a `kubectl get pdb -A` sweep during maintenance planning — it looks like a hard "no disruptions permitted" guarantee. It is actually an artifact of `desiredHealthy: 1` evaluated against zero pods. The workload has **no** disruption protection whatsoever.

Impact is a false signal to operators rather than lost redundancy (see Root Cause for why the distinction matters). Discovered during the 2026-08-06 cluster update-and-restart run documented in GUIDE-1070.

Two adjacent observations that are explicitly **not** this bug:

- `portfolio/phx-pdb` also reported `expectedPods: 0`, but it was **orphaned, not mis-selected** — no phx Deployment, StatefulSet, or pod existed anywhere, and `service/phx` selects `app=portfolio`, which `portfolio-pdb` already covers. **Resolved 2026-08-07: deleted.** Confirmed first against `nathanwhyte/nathanwhyte.dev` that its `k8s.yaml` ships only `portfolio-pdb`, that `phx` appears nowhere in that manifest, and that the deploy workflow never references a PDB.
- ⚠️ **`svc/phx` is NOT removable drift** — corrected 2026-08-09. Despite sharing the `phx` name and creation timestamp with the deleted PDB, it is the **live public entry point for the apex domain**: the cluster Cloudflare tunnel routes both `nathanwhyte.dev` and `www.nathanwhyte.dev` to `http://phx.portfolio.svc.cluster.local:80`. Deleting it would take the public site down. See Investigation Notes.
- `equal-risk/equal-risk-math` (also single-replica) has no PDB at all, which may well be intentional.

# Root Cause

A label-selector typo: the PDB was written against `app=rails` while the Deployment's pod template uses `app=equal-risk-rails`. Kubernetes does not warn about a PDB that selects nothing.

Two compounding factors:

1. **The resource is untracked.** It was created 2025-12-11T07:33:50Z and carries a `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation, but no PDB definition exists in `~/code/homelab` (a repo-wide grep for `PodDisruptionBudget` returns nothing) or in `~/code/equal-risk-portfolio`. It appears to have been applied ad hoc and has since drifted out of source control, so the typo was never reviewable in a diff.

2. **A single-replica Deployment cannot be protected by any PDB.** This is the key nuance and the reason severity is 2 rather than higher. A PDB constrains _simultaneous_ disruption across replicas; it cannot conjure availability that the replica count does not provide. With `replicas: 1`:
   - `minAvailable: 1` is unsatisfiable during eviction — the drain blocks forever rather than protecting anything.
   - `maxUnavailable: 1` permits the eviction, and the service is down for the reschedule.

   So the current outage behaviour would be identical if the PDB were deleted outright. What is actually broken is the _signal_, not the availability.

Note the maintenance script gets this right already: `pdb_preflight` in `scripts/node-maintenance.sh` intersects each PDB selector with pods actually on the target node, so it correctly stays silent for this PDB instead of reporting a phantom blocker.

# Investigation Notes

**2026-08-07** — Surfaced while correcting GUIDE-1070, which had claimed all three app PDBs (`equal-risk-pdb`, `phx-pdb`, `portfolio-pdb`) were single-replica drain-deadlock risks. Checking `status.expectedPods` showed only `portfolio-pdb` matches a pod.

Verified against the live cluster:

- `kubectl get pdb -n equal-risk equal-risk-pdb -o json` → selector `app=rails`, `expectedPods: 0`.
- `kubectl get deploy -n equal-risk` → `equal-risk-rails`, `replicas: 1`, pod template label `app=equal-risk-rails`.
- `kubectl delete pod -n equal-risk -l app=rails` during the 2026-08-06 run returned `No resources found`, which is what first exposed the mismatch.
- Repo-wide greps for `PodDisruptionBudget` / `equal-risk-pdb` across `~/code/homelab` and `~/code/equal-risk-portfolio` → no definition tracked anywhere.

Initially framed as "correct the selector"; revised after working through the replica arithmetic — a selector fix in isolation converts an inert PDB into a hard drain deadlock, which is strictly worse than today.

**2026-08-07 (later)** — Resolved the sibling `phx-pdb` question and deleted it. Sequence, for the record:

- Checked `nathanwhyte/nathanwhyte.dev` (the Phoenix/portfolio app repo) on the belief that `phx-pdb` might be required for its build or deploy. It is not: `k8s.yaml` declares exactly one PDB, `portfolio-pdb` (selector `app=portfolio`, `minAvailable: 1`); the string `phx` appears nowhere in that manifest; a repo-wide code search for `phx-pdb` returns nothing; and the deploy workflow `.github/workflows/build-hook.yaml` just calls a build hook with a bearer token, never touching `kubectl` or a PDB.
- Creation timestamps show a rename that left artifacts: `phx-pdb` and `svc/phx` both created 2026-01-28T06:19:18Z, superseded four days later by `portfolio-pdb` and `svc/portfolio` (2026-02-01T05:38:26Z). `svc/phx` had already been repointed to `app=portfolio` during that rename; the PDB's selector never was.
- Backed the resource up, then `kubectl delete pdb -n portfolio phx-pdb`. The portfolio Deployment

_The redirect to results after triggering a pipeline is inconsistently slow with no visual feedback._

---

# Symptom

After clicking "Run Pipeline" in the file upload modal, the trigger API call fires and eventually redirects to the results page. But the redirect speed is inconsistent — sometimes instant, sometimes several seconds. During the delay there's no spinner, loading overlay, or disabled state on the UI, so users can click elsewhere and interrupt the navigation.

# INFO-035 --- export_column_mappings_to_snowflake.py: Append-Not-Truncate Behavior

The column mappings exporter appends on every run and never truncates absent mapping types.

---

# Answer

- Exporter iterates only over `mapping_type.unique()` present in the current data.
- Never truncates tables for absent mapping types — if a mapping type is not in the current batch, its existing data is untouched.
- Appends on every run — no idempotency guarantee, leading to duplicate rows over time.
- Two schemas (`TEST__` prefix and non-prefix) are independently managed.

# Context

summary_cases.body_excerpt:
# BUG-1034 — OV sync overwrites pointer entries on cross-machine ID collision

Two machines intaking against unsynced compendium repos can allocate the same item ID, and because OpenViking pointer URIs are derived purely from the ID, whichever machine syncs last silently overwrites the other machine's OV entry.

---

# Problem

The vault is edited from two machines (work MacBook and pop), both committing to `main`. When machine B runs an intake before pulling machine A's pushed intake, `_scripts/next-id.sh` allocates the same ID (e.g. two different BUG-1035s) because it only scans the local working tree. Git then merges both files cleanly — the filenames differ by slug, so there is no merge conflict and nothing flags the duplicate ID. `compendium-sync.py` maps each file to its OpenViking URI from the entry ID alone, so both entries resolve to the same `viking://resources/compendium/...` pointer, and the last sync wins: one entry's OV pointer is silently overwritten and becomes unfindable via `viking_find`, letting duplicates slip through future intake checks.

Compounding this, OV syncs fire automatically as a non-blocking `nohup` step baked into the intake/completion/status-transition workflows, so the overwrite happens with no human in the loop and no visible error.

# Root Cause

Three interacting design gaps:

1. **Local-only ID allocation** — `_scripts/next-id.sh` computes the next ID by recursively scanning the local type directory plus `archive/{type}/`. It never fetches or consults `origin/main`, so any allocation on the remote that hasn't been pulled is invisible.
2. **ID-derived OV URIs with no overlap check** — `compendium-sync.py` `uri_for_path()` (`_scripts/compendium-sync.py:242`) builds the target URI as `{target_dir}{entry_id.lower()}.md`. The sync path calls `ov add-resource --to <uri>` without checking whether the URI already holds a pointer sourced from a *different* vault file.
3. **Automatic, silent sync trigger** — the intake/completion workflows queue the sync via `nohup ... --no-wait` with output appended to `/tmp/compendium-ov-sync.log`, so a collision overwrite produces no user-visible signal.

# Investigation Notes

- 2026-07-07 — Filed from first-principles review of the two-machine workflow (single `main` branch since IMPR-1010): no observed corrupted entry yet, but the mechanism is confirmed by reading `next-id.sh` (local-tree scan only) and `compendium-sync.py` (`uri_for_path` derives URIs from ID alone; `add-resource` overwrites). Duplicate vault IDs would also survive `git merge` because slugs differ.
- 2026-07-07 — Empirically reproduced all three mechanisms in a scratch clone (real vault + OV untouched):
  1. **Stale-tree reallocation**: with the just-filed BUG-1034 file removed (simulating a machine that never pulled it), `_scripts/next-id.sh BUG --scope personal` returned `BUG-1034` again instead of `BUG-1035`.
  2. **URI collision**: two files sharing `id: BUG-1034` with different slugs in `bugs/homelab/` both resolve via `uri_for_path()` to the identical URI `viking://resources/compendium/bugs/homelab/bug-1034.md` — last `add-resource` wins.
  3. **Clean merge**: two branches each intaking a distinct `BUG-1035` with different slugs merged with **no conflict**, leaving two files with one ID; the allocator then moved on to `BUG-1036`, permanently baking in the duplicate.
- 2026-07-07 — **Found an in-the-wild occurrence**: `_scripts/audit-organization.py` (which does detect `duplicate_ids`, but is not wired into pre-commit) reports a real pre-existing duplicate — `IMPR-104` existed as both `improvements/mage/IMPR-104-mage-fivetran-dev-environment-stub-for-aclaimant-source.md` and the session-logs improvement (then `improvements/other/IMPR-104-other-repurpose-today-week-as-session-logs.md`), both `date_created: 2026-06-29` in separate commits (`03ce6fc5` intake batch vs `e8540aa1` direct intake) — the parallel-intake signature exactly. Their OV URIs did **not** collide (different parent dirs, `improvements/mage/` vs `improvements/other/`), so no pointer was overwritten, but the ID-uniqueness invariant was broken. **Resolved 2026-07-07**: the session-logs entry — personal notes-workflow content that also should have been allocated in the personal band — was renumbered to [[IMPR-1041-other-repurpose-today-week-as-session-logs|IMPR-1041]] via `_scripts/renumber-item.py`; its research doc was renamed to match and all bare-ID references were rewritten. The 2026-07-05 OV-Reconcile entry in `log.md` records the duplicate as it stood at the time.
- 2026-07-07 — Scope note from testing: the OV overwrite only fires when the colliding entries land in the **same** vault subdirectory (URI includes the parent dir). Cross-directory duplicates "only" corrupt ID uniqueness and `viking_find` disambiguation. A fourth fix candidate: add `duplicate_ids` detection to pre-commit (today only the standalone audit script catches it, and only when run by hand).

# Fix

Implementation plan: [[docs/plans/2026-07-07-BUG-1034-ov-sync-id-collision-fixes|2026-07-07 OV sync ID-collision fixes]] (3 phases covering items 1–3 below; item 3 executes as an on-demand Job in a new `compendium` k3s namespace, making the cluster the single sync writer).

All four fixes shipped (2026-07-07/08):

1. ✅ **Remote-aware ID allocation** (`1033faae`) — `next-id.sh` fetches `origin/main` and takes the max across local and remote trees; loud divergence/offline warnings; `NEXT_ID_NO_FETCH=1` escape hatch. `compendium-new --help` documents it (dotfiles `e5b3433`).
2. ✅ **Pre-sync overlap check** (`37160506`) — before `add-resource`, the sync reads the existing pointer's `Path:` provenance line; cross-source mismatches are refused (interactive y/N locally; loud Job failure in-cluster), `--force-overlap` for deliberate repairs, `--no-overlap-check` for bulk reconciles. Retry hardening for `Resource is being processed` conflicts in `2bf8bd68`.
3. ✅ **Manual sync trigger** (`38b9365d`; homelab `2762619`/`f06369

# INFO-095 — Liberty RiskTrac record types and source_file_names structure

_How Liberty RiskTrac fixed-width files are structured and how the `source_file_names` table maps record types to Snowflake tables._

# File Format

Liberty RiskTrac files are multi-record-type fixed-width text files. Each line starts with a 2-character record type prefix. The `liberty_risktrac` loader parses these into separate Snowflake tables based on the prefix.

## Record Type Prefixes

| Prefix | Meaning | Snowflake table(s) | Line of business |
|---|---|---|---|
| WC | Workers compensation claim | wc_01 (main), wc_03, wc_05, wc_06 | Workers comp |
| VB | Vehicle/bodily injury claim | pal_01 (main), pal_03 | Property/auto/liability |
| EM | Employers liability claim | pal_01 (main), pal_03 | Property/auto/liability |
| WP | Workers comp policy | wc_01 | Workers comp |
| VH | Vehicle header | pal_01 | Property/auto/liability |
| VC | Vehicle claim | pal_01 | Property/auto/liability |
| (header) | Control totals / file header | control_totals_00 | N/A |

The first line (no prefix / spaces) is the control totals record with aggregate financial data.

## Record Type Counts (CIC Helmsmann example)

| Prefix | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| WC | 5,353 | Bulk of the file |
| VB | 2,341 | Second largest |
| EM | 1,013 | Employers liability |
| WP | 24 | Policy records |
| VH | 17 | Vehicle headers |
| VC | 6 | Vehicle claims |

# source_file_names Structure

Both claims and policy pipelines use the **same 10-entry structure**. The only difference is `data_type`:

| table_name | data_type (claims) | data_type (policy) | main_table |
|---|---|---|---|
| claims | claims | policies | — |
| wc_01 | claims | policies | — |
| wc_03 | claims | policies | — |
| wc_05 | null | null | wc_01 |
| wc_06 | null | null | wc_01 |
| pal_01 | claims | policies | — |
| pal_03 | claims | policies | — |
| pal_04 | null | null | pal_01 |
| pal_05 | null | null | pal_01 |
| control_totals_00 | claims | policies | — |

Key rules:

- `table_name` stays as `claims` on the main entry — even for policy pipelines. The Liberty RiskTrac loader creates `RAW_DATA_CLAIMS` regardless of pipeline type.
- `data_type` = `"policies"` on main tables, `null` on sub-tables (entries with `main_table` set)
- `main_table` links sub-tables to their parent (e.g., `pal_04` → `pal_01`)
- All entries use the same `source_file_name` pattern

# Common Mistakes

- Setting `table_name` to `"POLICIES"` or `"policies"` — causes `RAW_DATA_POLICIES does not exist` error (ERR-042)
- Using only 1 source_file_name entry (like CoWorx's `fixed_width` pipeline) — Liberty RiskTrac needs all 10
- Missing `.txt` extension on the source_file_name pattern (ERR-040)
